assessment: This article reports a significant discovery: disrupting the function of the tyramine receptor in honey bees causes a rapid decline in their responses to olfactory stimuli. This finding highlights the important role of tyramine receptors, one of the most highly expressed biogenic amine receptors in the insect olfactory system. The authors propose that tyramine signaling may specifically control the process of latent inhibition, but the evidence presented does not rule out the possibility that tyramine affects other functions of the antennal lobe.
